description:
`scripts/cargo-ci.sh` serialises runs under a host lock (`CARGO_CI_BUILD_LOCK`). With per-test limits and the host's shared cargo jobserver pool, two runs may coexist. This measures whether they do.

## Background

The host runs a cargo jobserver pool (`cargo-pool-daemon`) that shares cores between concurrent cargo invocations. Today `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` takes a host-wide lock, so authoritative gate runs from several leads queue one after another.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A committed benchmark note records at least three trials of two `cargo-ci` runs started together under the pool on different worktrees, with the per-test limits enforced and the lock bypassed. Each trial reports each run's verdict, any per-test limit failures, and both runs' wall-clock durations against a serial baseline.
- [hard] REQ-02: The note states a decision with its evidence: the lock is removed, if every trial passes with no limit failure, or kept, naming the failure mode observed.
- [hard] REQ-03: If the decision is to remove the lock, `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` no longer takes it, and its header and the `cargo-ci` gate description say so. If the decision is to keep it, nothing changes outside the note.

## Decisions

- D-01: If every trial passes with no per-test limit failure, `scripts/cargo-ci.sh` drops the host lock (user ruling, 2026-11-03), knowing the cargo jobserver pool exists only on this host.

## Notes

Run the trials when no lead's gates are queued.
title: Decide whether concurrent cargo-ci runs can drop the host lock
